question: What does error KST-2044 mean and how do I fix it?

evidence.quote: the Kestrel addresses are missing from it
add both 203.0.113.10 and 203.0.113.11 to the allowlist

expected_answer: The data source refused the connection because the Kestrel IP addresses are not on its allowlist. Add both 203.0.113.10 and 203.0.113.11; adding only one causes intermittent errors.
notes: Neighbour code KST-2040 (timeout) is semantically very close. Watch whether retrieval returns the wrong code.

question: A user gets KST-4012 when accepting an invitation. What should support tell them?

evidence.quote: all seats of the plan are already used
an Admin of the workspace must remove a member to free a seat, or the Owner must add seats or move to a larger plan

expected_answer: There is no free seat. An Admin must free a seat, or the Owner must add seats or upgrade. The same invitation then works if it is less than 7 days old.
notes: Exact code lookup. The product guide (section 4) also covers the situation without the code.

question: What happens, step by step, when a customer's card payment fails?

evidence.quote: We then retry the payment automatically 1 day, 3 days and 7 days after the first attempt
a grace period of 21 days from the first failed attempt
the workspace becomes read-only
60 days after the first failed attempt, the workspace is suspended

expected_answer: E-mail to the Owner and billing contact, retries after 1, 3 and 7 days, then a 21-day grace period (everything works), then read-only, then suspension at 60 days. Nothing is deleted.
notes: Spread over several paragraphs: with small chunks, top-k rarely covers all of it. Also a version trap: the 2025 policy has 2 retries and a 14-day grace period.

question: Which plans include single sign-on, and how does an admin set it up?

evidence.quote: | Single sign-on (SAML) | — | — | — | Yes | Yes |
downloads the Kestrel service provider metadata

expected_answer: Business and Enterprise. An Admin opens Settings → Security → Single sign-on, downloads the Kestrel SP metadata, registers Kestrel in the identity provider, pastes the IdP metadata URL back, tests with one Admin, then enforces it.
notes: One half is a table row, far from the setup paragraph. Tables also chunk badly.

question: I lost my phone and I can't log in anymore. What can I do?

evidence.quote: If you no longer have your authenticator device, use one of your backup codes
ask an Admin of your workspace to reset your second factor

expected_answer: Use a backup code. Without one, ask a workspace Admin to reset your second factor. If you are the only Admin or the Owner, contact support from the account's e-mail address; identity verification can take up to 2 business days.
notes: The documents never say 'phone' or 'log in' here: they say 'authenticator device', 'sign in', 'second factor'.

question: Can I get a refund on my annual plan 45 days after it renewed?

evidence.quote: within 60 days of the purchase or renewal date
pro-rated from the date of the request

expected_answer: Yes, under the current (March 2026) policy: annual plans are refundable within 60 days of renewal, pro-rated from the request date. The old 2025 policy allowed only 30 days.
notes: The 2025 policy says 30 days and answers 'no'. Both versions are nearly identical text, so they get very similar embeddings.

question: How much do I save by paying annually instead of monthly?

evidence.quote: Customers who choose annual billing receive a 20% discount

expected_answer: 20% compared with twelve months of monthly billing (it was 15% under the 2025 policy).

question: A customer gets KST-2044. Which team owns the Kestrel service that the IP addresses to allowlist belong to?

evidence.quote: add both 203.0.113.10 and 203.0.113.11 to the allowlist
All outgoing connections leave through two fixed addresses, 203.0.113.10 and 203.0.113.11.

expected_answer: Data Integrations: the addresses 203.0.113.10 and 203.0.113.11 are the outgoing addresses of connector-hub, which Data Integrations owns.
notes: Added for V3 (new two_hop question). Hop 1 (runbook): KST-2044 -> the two IP addresses. Hop 2 (service catalog): those addresses -> connector-hub -> Owner: Data Integrations (the owner line is in the same section as the quote). The question names neither connector-hub nor the team; the runbook says 'Escalate: no' for KST-2044, so the answer is only reachable through the catalog.
